source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I can see that the inner-layer copper pours are carrying the bulk of the load, but I specifically want to verify two points for VBUS and BAT− because they have the highest worst-case current (up to ~1.5 A: 1 A charging + ~0.5 A system load simultaneously):
Do the [URL_019] / [URL_020] pours remain continuous from [CLIENT_NAME_002]-C / battery connector through to the AXP2101 VBUS / BAT pins, without any thin trace acting as a series bottleneck?
Is there enough stitching between [URL_019] and [URL_020] on those nets (typically 3+ vias for ~1.5 A)?
If the answer to both is yes, I’m satisfied. My concern is only if a 0.2 mm bottleneck exists somewhere in series, since 1.5 A through a 0.2 mm outer trace would make it run hot (~30 °C rise above ambient).

value_updates.worst_case_current: ~1.5 A (1 A charging plus approximately 0.5 A system load)
value_updates.current_path_requirement: Copper pours must remain continuous from the USB-C or battery connector through to the corresponding AXP2101 VBUS or BAT pin.
value_updates.series_bottleneck_prohibition: No thin trace, including a 0.2 mm trace, may act as a series bottleneck.
value_updates.stitching_requirement: Provide sufficient interlayer stitching on the high-current nets, typically at least 3 vias for approximately 1.5 A.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: Regarding the battery traces, they are currently able to carry 2.5A without any problem.
